subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Which external capture contract should Birdclaw commit to supporting in core, and what provenance and completeness guarantees must be stored for imported records?
rationale: Current architecture provides reusable canonical persistence, but code inspection cannot determine whether Birdclaw should permanently support one versioned producer, multiple evolving formats, or only a documented conversion boundary.

options.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
options.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and partial-completeness metadata, while deferring legacy and twitter-web-exporter shapes.

options.title: Support all proposed formats
options.body: Commit the first implementation to Scrollmark canonical and legacy files plus twitter-web-exporter, accepting a broader compatibility and fixture-maintenance burden.

options.title: Require canonical conversion
options.body: Keep third-party schemas outside core and document a conversion tool or intermediate Birdclaw-owned import envelope.

recommendation.title: Start with Scrollmark v1
recommendation.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and partial-completeness metadata, while deferring legacy and twitter-web-exporter shapes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects Birdclaw’s product boundary, persistent schema, and canonical import semantics represented in the vision and recent storage work.
